summary: Ground Radar is a web app that turns NASA Earth observation data, local soil surveys, and smartphone photos into simple, two-year crop rotation plans. Today, shifting weather patterns, water shortages, and declining soil health make it hard for growers to know what to plant. Satellite pixels cover huge areas and miss small details on the ground, while raw climate data is too confusing for everyday users. Our platform solves this by letting users trace their exact field on a map, upload three to six soil photos, and set personal goals like saving water or rebuilding topsoil. Ground Radar combines NASA rainfall, temperature, soil moisture, and elevation data with USDA soil maps and AI photo checks to build three ranked rotation plans, an interactive Field Agronomist chat-box, and a two-year seasonal simulation. This matters because it makes complex space science easy to use, helping farmers, backyard gardeners, and students protect their soil, save water, and grow stronger crops.
details:
Project Details Ground Radar is a decision-support web app built for commercial farmers, first-time growers, community gardeners, and students learning sustainable agriculture.

How It Works:

  1. Trace Your Plot: Users draw the boundary of their farm field or garden on a satellite map to measure exact coordinates and acreage.
  2. Ground-Truth Survey: Users upload three to six photos of their soil from different angles and adjust priority sliders for water savings, soil health, pest reduction, and harvest yield.
  3. Space + Soil + Vision Synthesis: Our backend pulls live NASA climate, soil moisture, and terrain data alongside USDA soil surveys. Multimodal AI inspects the uploaded photos to spot surface crusting, standing puddles, or leftover weeds that coarse satellite pixels miss.
  4. Actionable Plans, Chat & Simulation: Users get plain-English soil and frost health cards, three ranked two-year crop rotation plans, an AI Field Agronomist chat-box grounded in their exact plot data, and a week-by-week two-year simulation to test seasonal resilience.

Benefits & Intended Impact: Instead of guessing what to plant next, growers get clear, personalized planting windows and cover-crop pairings that prevent nutrient depletion, cut unnecessary irrigation, and break pest cycles. By translating complicated telemetry into everyday language, Ground Radar lowers the barrier to regenerative farming.

Tools, Languages & Software Used: We built Ground Radar using React, TypeScript, and Vite, hosted on Vercel, with Supabase (PostgreSQL, Auth, and Storage) for cloud persistence. We integrated Mapbox GL for satellite field tracing, NASA APIs (POWER, SMAP/MERRA-2, SRTM, GIBS), USDA NRCS SSURGO and ISRIC SoilGrids for soil profiles, and Gemini 2.5 Flash for multimodal photo analysis and agronomist Q&A.

Creativity & Factors Considered: Our biggest creative breakthrough was pairing orbital satellite pixels with phone camera photos so coarse space data gets calibrated to centimeter-level soil conditions. We also considered real-world constraints like mobile loading speed (using fast parallel API calls), regional soil coverage (adding a global SoilGrids backup outside the U.S.), and user experience (designing a jargon-free interface with a guest demo mode).

Deployed Web-APP Link: https://groundradar-5lh7-dpai8aecf-tiyags-projects.vercel.app
